solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dropping sadly can limit cacti in development

indicators.note: something in development is still changing shape, so the letters are not yet in their final order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A gardener watches a stunted cactus collection fail to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: an anticlimax is a let-down that comes just when things were building up.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: an anticlimactic moment is a disappointing drop after rising expectation.

clue.text: Where hands go through three consecutive eight-hour shifts?

definitions.meaning: the surface reads hands as workers clocking on; the setter means the pointers on a dial, and where they travel
three eight-hour shifts in a row make up a full 24 hours, the time those pointers take to go round twice

explanation.surface: A factory rota keeps the workforce busy day and night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' reads as workers on shifts, but clock hands literally travel around the clock, and a 24-hour rota runs around the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom read literally: working around the clock means non-stop, and clock hands physically go around the clock.

clue.text: Tons persistently worry over nasal sound

parts.note: t = tons

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word turned over is upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to gnaw at is to worry persistently

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a whining noise from their own nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persistently worry' looks like NAG, but it is GNAW, which reversed gives the WANG you need.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a twang is the resonant, through-the-nose quality of some voices and accents.

clue.text: What could be sharp chintz raincoat child's regularly taken out

indicators.note: letters removed at regular intervals means every other one goes

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of these three words, read in order

explanation.surface: A child's garish flowered raincoat has been taken out of the wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' means sour-tasting here, not stylish, so the definition is a cautious 'could be': citric acid is one sharp thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: citric acid is what makes lemons taste sharp, so it is one thing that could be sharp.

clue.text: Foolishness and madness banishing son

indicators.note: to banish is to send away, so the son is removed from the word

parts.note: insanity = madness
s = son, removed

explanation.surface: A family drama in which a father's folly ends with his son thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the wordplay nearly mean the same thing, which makes 'and' a natural join.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: inanity is empty-headed silliness.

clue.text: Pure northern Gaelic must be translated

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, and here the letters are turned into another word

parts.note: n = northern
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A purist insists that a Highland text be rendered faithfully into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' is natural next to a language name, which hides its job of rearranging letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: angels stand for innocence, so angelic means pure.

clue.text: One securing rank

definitions.meaning: someone who ties things fast, the -er agent noun of 'tie'
a row or level in a stepped arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone clinches a promotion to a higher grade.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the made-up-looking 'one who ties'; crosswords lean on these -ER agent nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a crossword-only agent noun, one who ties, and the ordinary word for a row or level.

clue.text: Star locked up by prison governor

indicators.note: something locked up by another is held inside it, so the star sits within the prison

parts.note: can = prison (slang)
stella is Latin for star, and a name

explanation.surface: A celebrity is jailed on the orders of the man who runs the prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison governor' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'prison' is CAN in the wordplay and 'governor' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific kind of governor: a castellan was the official in charge of a castle.

clue.text: Is Carmine gored getting involved in this?

definitions.text: Is Carmine gored getting involved in this?

indicators.note: things that get involved become tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

explanation.surface: A gangster called Carmine gets stabbed after mixing with the Mob.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmine is a stock mobster's name, and getting gored is what happens to someone who gets mixed up with the Mafia.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: a Carmine getting knifed is just the fate you would expect from involvement in the Mafia world.

clue.text: Illusory images of neutrino particles?

indicators.note: The answer is made of part of the words that follow, a run of letters within them.

parts.note: the letters run on unbroken across the words

explanation.surface: A physicist asks whether pictures of subatomic particles are real.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the answer is not really about physics: it runs from the last letter of 'neutrino' into 'particles'.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: op art is abstract art whose patterns create optical illusions.

clue.text: Gross rage is out of order for assailant

indicators.note: things out of order are not in the right sequence, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A disapproving verdict on someone's violent temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' reads as a British reproach, meaning unacceptable, rather than a signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the aggressor is the one who attacks first.

clue.text: Unimportant note, for instance, readable with a typo?

parts.note: EG, exempli gratia, means for instance

indicators.note: a typing slip has changed one letter of the word for readable to another

parts.note: readable writing is legible

explanation.surface: A note that is perfectly readable apart from one misprint is hardly worth worrying about.
explanation.walkthrough: The typo turns the first E of LEGIBLE into I, giving LIGIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something negligible is so small or trivial that it can be ignored.

clue.text: Letter of thanks after Beeb has abolished repeats

indicators.note: one piece placed after another comes later in the answer

parts.note: BEEB with its doubled letters removed leaves B and E once each
ta = thanks

explanation.surface: A thank-you note to the BBC after it stops showing reruns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is a nickname for the BBC, and 'repeats' are reruns in the surface but repeated letters in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Excitedly waves health food recipes

parts.note: bran is a classic health food
dishes = recipes

explanation.surface: An enthusiast holds up a wholefood cookbook.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'health food recipes' as one phrase; it splits after 'food'.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to brandish something is to wave it about with a flourish.

clue.text: Scrap, a bit of thin muslin

parts.note: a scrap is a quarrel, a tiff
'any' = a bit of, as in 'have you any milk?'

explanation.surface: A seamstress offers a small offcut of fine fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' wants to be a scrap of cloth, beside muslin; it is a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An old dictionary sense: tiffany is a gauzy, thin muslin fabric.

clue.text: Forcibly move ornamental coat fastener on border

parts.note: a frog is a looped braid fastening on a coat
a march is a frontier or border region

explanation.surface: A tailor's instruction to shift a decorative button along the edge of a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the fastener above the border.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to frogmarch someone is to force them along with their arms held.

clue.text: Italian composer writes music endlessly, flipping bad

indicators.note: without its ends, so the first and last letters of the word go

parts.note: a composer scores a piece

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for bad round to run backwards

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: An Italian composer writes music non-stop and things go badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping applies only to the word for bad; the music word is simply trimmed at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was a Baroque violinist and composer from Italy.

clue.text: Gradually losing stone, say, cut by sculptor

indicators.note: something cut by a blade has the blade inside it, so the sculptor goes into the middle

parts.note: e.g. = say, for example
Auguste Rodin, the French sculptor

explanation.surface: A sculptor chisels a block down bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay: rock that is eroding is gradually losing stone, and 'say' on its own gives EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: erosion is rock worn away little by little.

clue.text: Dumplings — no small volume covered in butter

indicators.note: the butter wraps around the other letters, so they are covered in it

parts.note: ghi, also spelt ghee, is the clarified butter of Indian cooking
CC, cubic centimetres, is a small measure of volume

explanation.surface: A cook insists the dumplings should be smothered in butter, and not just a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings made from potato, semolina or flour.

clue.text: Atonement not unknown in pirates' home

indicators.note: 'not unknown' means without the unknown, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: The Pirates of Penzance, Gilbert and Sullivan's opera; Penzance is a Cornish town
z = an unknown in algebra, removed

explanation.surface: Buccaneers find no forgiveness back at base.
explanation.walkthrough: Algebra's unknowns are X, Y and Z; here it has to be Z. 'Not unknown' also reads as a double negative, which hides the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: penance is punishment undertaken to make amends for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Delay Broadway's opening of play around November

indicators.note: one thing around another encloses it

parts.note: the American spelling of prologue, so Broadway's version
N = November in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A theatre postpones its New York premiere until the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadway's opening' tempts you to take B; Broadway is only there to make the prologue American, PROLOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to prolong something is to drag it out, delaying its end.

clue.text: What's used to catch birds in tree

definitions.meaning: a sticky paste smeared on branches so perching birds are stuck

explanation.surface: A bird-catcher sets a trap up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Birdlime was spread on twigs so perching birds stuck fast, hence 'lime' as a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: short for birdlime, the old sticky trap, and another name for the linden tree.

clue.text: Big and impenetrable loch I'm into, swimming

indicators.note: things swimming move about freely, so the letters shift position

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A wild swimmer boasts about a vast, murky Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big and impenetrable' could describe the loch itself, which hides that it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a monolith is a single massive block of stone, so monolithic means huge and seamless.

clue.text: Port city of Nova Scotia unfinished and not large

indicators.note: not says the large abbreviation is left out
unfinished means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Halifax is the capital city of the Canadian province of Nova Scotia
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A Canadian port city lies half-built and small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port city' looks like the definition, but 'city of Nova Scotia' is the wordplay and 'Port' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a major seaport on the Mediterranean coast of northern Israel.

clue.text: Cross about book being forbidden

indicators.note: one thing about another surrounds it, so the cross goes round the book

parts.note: a tau cross is T-shaped
b = book

explanation.surface: Someone is angry that a book has been banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the T-shaped tau cross. TABU is a variant spelling of taboo.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling: tabu is taboo, the word for something banned by custom.

clue.text: Hors d'œuvre of fish I love after starters of artisanal cold cuts

indicators.note: I and love come after the opening letters in the answer

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the opening letters of each of the following words are the starters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero is O

explanation.surface: Someone loves a starter of fish after some craft-made cold meats.
explanation.walkthrough: CARP, then ACC from the first letters of artisanal cold cuts, then I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpaccio is a starter of very thinly sliced raw meat or fish.

clue.text: West end of Hispaniola island — not all of it?

definitions.text: West end of Hispaniola island — not all of it?

indicators.note: in an across answer the west end of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A question about the country that takes up the western part of Hispaniola, which is not the whole island.
explanation.walkthrough: H, then AIT, then IT cut short to I. Read whole, the clue also describes the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is the nation occupying the western third of the Caribbean island of Hispaniola.

clue.text: Washing car outside university residential area

indicators.note: one word outside another encloses it, so the washing goes round the university

parts.note: hosing down = washing
u = university
an estate car is the British name for a station wagon

explanation.surface: Someone hoses down their car outside the student halls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washing car' reads as one activity, and 'outside university' as a location; both split, with 'outside' telling the washing to wrap the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term: a housing estate is a planned development of homes built together.
